decisions.reason: Report connects plugin/lib/client.js's top-level ESM import to host-boot-log.txt's single classic-script combo and browser-error.txt's compile failure: one syntax error fails the whole combo parse, so zero entries register and the stock plugins disappear. It explicitly identifies the named @deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-registry entry as merely the first awaited victim of the shared combo failure while the diagnostic payload points at the dsh-profiles bundle, and it scopes the classic-script grammar conclusion to this combo rather than all JavaScript loading.

Report prescribes bisecting the cordis.patch.yml insert rows to implicate the newest plugin and a static classic-script parse check (node --check as a script plus top-level import/export scan) rather than trusting the named entry. It describes the working-plugin packaging from working-plugin-excerpt.txt: window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory}) with the plugin's package-name id, CJS module/exports body, host-provided React and react-dom obtained via require inside the factory, and inject/apply exposed on module.exports. It only borrows the shell, not the elided bodies.

Report correctly uses plugin-apply-error.txt and the bare ctx.slots.register call to explain the two-sided slot graph: the parent settings entry owns the settings.section declaration and the new plugin may only contribute children, and the apply failure is scoped to @lhh010/dsh-profiles while others load. However, it never states that apply ordering is not guaranteed, and it only names the ctx.slots.inject form without showing or precisely describing the deferred callback (inject returning/waiting on the registration) the contract requires. It also wrongly forbids the registrant from passing name, whereas registrants supply name/id/order while kind/scope stay declaration-owned.

Grounded in host-boot-log.txt and restart-notes.txt: the combo is assembled once per host boot from disk, so file edits and browser hard refreshes keep serving the stale combo; each iteration requires a full host stop and restart followed by refresh and a Plugin-list check. EADDRINUSE is explained as the orphaned old node process still holding the listening port after the terminal was closed, fixed by killing the whole tree with taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F, not as a packaging defect of the new plugin.

Proposes host-side per-plugin classic-script validation before composing the combo with culprit attribution to the owning plugin id/path instead of the first awaited entry, plus apply-time slot-registration validation attributed to the registering entry. The authoring checklist covers the loader factory wrapper, no top-level import/export with host React via require, inject/apply exports, deferred cross-entry contributions via ctx.slots.inject to parent-declared slots without redeclaring kind/scope, and the restart/taskkill/refresh/verify dev loop — not a generic add-tests list.

caps.reason: All final advice aligns with the incident contracts: remove top-level ESM from the classic combo, use ctx.slots.inject for cross-entry contributions, keep kind/scope declaration-owned, and require a full host restart (with Windows tree kill) rather than HMR or browser refresh.
